headline: Retired Rescue Dog Wins Award for Sniffing Out Sea Invader
meta_description: Sgiath, a former mountain rescue Labrador, has won IFAW's Animal of the Year for pioneering work detecting invasive sea creatures.
summary_short: A retired mountain rescue dog named Sgiath has become the first canine trained to detect invasive 'sea vomit,' earning conservation recognition.
body:
A former mountain rescue Labrador named Sgiath has won IFAW's Animal of the Year award for groundbreaking conservation work. The dog is believed to be the first of its kind trained to sniff out invasive sea vomit, helping scientists and conservationists combat the spread of this unwanted marine species.

Sgiath's transition from mountain rescue to marine conservation represents an innovative approach to protecting coastal ecosystems. By detecting the presence of invasive organisms before they spread, the dog's work supports efforts to preserve delicate environmental balance and prevent ecological damage.

The award recognizes that animal contributions to conservation extend far beyond traditional wildlife roles. Sgiath's story demonstrates how trained animals can become unexpected allies in the fight against invasive species, bringing both scientific value and public attention to environmental challenges.
quick_facts: Former mountain rescue dog Sgiath won IFAW's Animal of the Year
First dog trained to detect invasive 'sea vomit' species
Now works with conservationists on marine ecosystem protection
